resources.string: Choose \'Off\' to switch screens instantly with no animation. If the speed is too fast, some apps may flicker or look frozen. If that happens, go back to 0.5× or the default. GOAT\'s droplet animations also follow this setting.

GOAT changes this with the same system settings permission as Advanced Display Scale, and it stays after a reboot. If you turn off Developer options, the device resets these to default, but GOAT reapplies your choice.

These are the same as \'Window animation scale\', \'Transition animation scale\', and \'Animator duration scale\' in Developer options. Picking one value changes all three. Expand \'%1$s\' to adjust each one separately.
Changes how fast animations play when you open or close apps and switch screens. At 0.5×, animations finish in half the time and feel faster. 0.5× is the most popular choice.
If turned off, you can\'t customize AR Emoji.
If turned off, you can\'t create AR Emoji.
If turned off, the AR feature hub, including AR Emoji and AR Doodle, goes away.
If turned off, you can\'t use Bixby Vision (object recognition) in the camera.
If turned off, you can\'t use Bixby voice commands. First set the side button\'s press-and-hold action to \'Power off menu\'.
If turned off, you can\'t call Bixby by saying \'Hi Bixby\'.
If turned off, Samsung Cloud backup and sync stop.
%1$s You can turn it back on anytime.
If turned off, you can\'t run two copies of a messaging app. Leave it on if you use a second copy.
If turned off, the lock screen wallpaper no longer changes automatically.
If turned off, the \'People\' panel disappears from Edge panels.
If turned off, you can\'t use the Samsung Email app.
Component that auto-updates the Facebook app.
Component that preinstalls the Facebook app.
If turned off, the game library and in-game toolbar go away.
If turned off, in-game performance limits are lifted, but heat and battery drain may increase. On some devices, it turns back on after a reboot.

Apps are set to \'Disabled\' instead of being uninstalled. This doesn\'t free up storage, but you can turn them back on anytime with the switch. For apps marked \'Caution\', GOAT explains what changes before you turn them off.
Turning built-in apps on and off requires PC-level (ADB) permission. Once Shizuku is connected, GOAT uses that permission to turn apps on and off.
Some apps, like Game Optimizing Service, turn back on after an update or reboot. GOAT checks their status every time you open this screen, so turn them off again if they\'re back on.

Turn off built-in Samsung and partner apps you don\'t use to remove them from your app list, notifications, and background activity. The list only includes apps that don\'t affect core features like calls, messages, Settings, and the camera.
If turned off, you can\'t use Samsung Internet. Set another browser as your default first.
If turned off, you can\'t use Kids mode.
If turned off, you can\'t install or use Kids mode.
If turned off, you can\'t use the LinkedIn app.
If turned off, you can\'t use Samsung Members, the error reporting and community app.
Component that preinstalls Netflix. The Netflix app itself is not affected.
If turned off, you can\'t use Microsoft OneDrive.
Only needed to move data from another phone. Turn it back on when you need to transfer data.
If turned off, the feed to the left of the Home screen goes away.
If turned off, you can\'t download extra stickers for the camera and keyboard.
If turned off, the Samsung Tips app and its notifications go away.
Component turned off together with Bixby Vision.
If turned off, you can\'t use Samsung Pay payments, transit cards, or memberships. Leave it on if you use it to pay.
If turned off, the apps needed to connect a Galaxy Watch or Buds won\'t install automatically.

Because the system recolors other apps on its own, some screens may look off. For example, the status bar text and icons may stay black on a dark background, or a white box may appear behind Home screen folders. GOAT can\'t fix this, so turn off the switch if it bothers you. Turning it off restores the original look.

This setting turns off after a reboot. If you leave the switch on, GOAT turns it back on once after each boot, when Shizuku connects. If you turned it off yourself in Developer options after booting, GOAT leaves it off.
There\'s no official way to choose apps one by one, so it applies to every app without dark mode support. Apps that block force dark and apps with their own dark mode don\'t change.

Android only applies force dark while system dark mode is on. So if dark mode is off when you turn on the switch, GOAT turns dark mode on too. When you turn the switch off, dark mode goes back to how it was (off, auto, or scheduled). Apps that are already running need to be reopened.
The system shows apps that don\'t support dark mode in dark colors too. It\'s the same as \'Override force-dark\' in Developer options, and it doesn\'t change the colors of photos or videos.

Doze turns back on after a reboot. If you turned it off here, GOAT turns it off again once after each boot, when Shizuku connects. If you turned it back on yourself, such as from a PC, after booting, GOAT leaves it on.

Notifications and background tasks are delayed less. However, apps keep running while the screen is off, so standby battery drain increases significantly. If only certain apps send late notifications, it\'s better to set that app\'s battery setting to \'Unrestricted\'.
This requires PC-level (ADB) permission, so GOAT turns it on and off with Shizuku. Turning off the switch turns Doze back on. From a PC, you can undo it with \'adb shell dumpsys deviceidle enable\'.

When your phone sits with the screen off, Android saves battery by batching apps\' background activity and network use. This is called Doze, and it can make messenger and email notifications arrive late. This feature turns Doze off.

On some devices, GOS turns back on after an update or reboot. If you leave the switch on, GOAT checks once after each boot, when Shizuku connects, and turns it off again. If you turned it back on yourself, such as in Settings, after booting, GOAT leaves it on.

With the performance limits gone, long play sessions make your phone run hotter and drain the battery faster. If it gets too hot, the system lowers performance. Game Launcher and Game Booster stay as they are.
Turning off the switch turns GOS back on. It\'s the same setting as \'Game Optimizing Service (GOS)\' in Bloatware Cleanup, so the result is the same whichever screen you change it from.

Game Optimizing Service (GOS) is a Samsung service that lowers resolution, frame rate, and processing power during games to reduce heat and battery drain. Turning it off stops this throttling, which may improve performance in the same game. Results vary by device and game.

In Power saving mode, at very low brightness, and in some game and video apps, the system lowers the refresh rate temporarily. Once that ends, it goes back to the mode you chose. A locked refresh rate stays after a reboot.

\'%1$s\' raises the refresh rate only when the screen moves and lowers it when still. \'%2$s\' keeps the highest refresh rate even on a still screen, for the fastest touch response. This option shows your device\'s top rate, like \'Always 120Hz\'. \'%3$s\' locks to 60Hz to save battery.

The max and min refresh rates are hidden system settings, so GOAT changes them with Shizuku. Choosing \'%1$s\' restores the values from before GOAT changed them. You can also change it in Settings → Display → \'Motion smoothness\'. GOAT doesn\'t overwrite values changed outside the app.
The number of times the screen refreshes per second. 120Hz refreshes twice as often as 60Hz, making scrolling and motion smoother. In exchange, it uses a bit more battery.

After a change, the screen flickers briefly and a \'%2$s\' window appears for %1$d s. If you don\'t tap [%3$s] in time, it goes back to the original. If you reboot before confirming, it also goes back on the next boot.
Fold isn\'t supported because it\'s unclear how the two screens store their resolutions separately. Resolution is changed with the same system settings permission as Advanced Display Scale.

To keep on-screen elements the same size, GOAT lowers the screen density (DPI) by the same ratio and matches Advanced Display Scale too. Apps with a per-app scale only allow fixed steps in Samsung settings, so they look slightly larger while the resolution is lowered.

Choosing \'Original\' restores the resolution from before GOAT changed it. If you had lowered it to FHD+ in Samsung settings, it goes back to FHD+. If the screen becomes unusable, run \'%1$s\' from a PC.
Reduces only the screen\'s pixel count, keeping text and icon sizes the same. Sharpness drops slightly, but games may run at higher frame rates or use less battery. Results vary by device and app.
On some devices, the forced shutter sound setting may turn back on after an update or reboot. If you leave the switch on, GOAT checks each time Shizuku connects and turns it off again.
The shutter sound exists to prevent illegal filming. Filming others without consent is punishable by law. Use this only for courtesy, like photographing objects, documents, or food in quiet places.
Turning off the switch makes the shutter sound always play again. From a PC, you can undo it with \'%1$s\'.

Galaxy phones sold in Korea always play a shutter sound, even in Silent or Vibrate mode. Turning this setting off makes the shutter sound follow your device\'s sound settings, so photos are taken silently in Silent or Vibrate mode. It works in the Samsung Camera app and most other camera apps.

The forced shutter sound is a hidden Samsung system setting, so even the system settings permission can\'t change it. GOAT changes it through Shizuku. If you don\'t use Shizuku, you can also run a command once from a PC.
Now a shake slightly weaker than the one you just did will rotate the screen.
Move your device and the droplet moves too.
Tap [Start] and shake as usual for %1$d s.
When an app sets the screen orientation, like full-screen video, the screen follows it. When you close that app, it returns to your locked orientation.

\'Shake to Rotate\' works while Auto rotate is off. When you turn this on, GOAT turns off Auto rotate and locks the screen in its current orientation. If you turned Auto rotate back on from Quick settings, tap [%1$s] on this screen.

Shakes are detected only with the accelerometer, and the sensor isn\'t used while the screen is off, so battery use is minimal. Android stops sensor access for apps without a notification, so one GOAT notification must stay visible. If another GOAT notification is showing, GOAT uses it; otherwise, it shows one with no sound or vibration.

Sensitivity ranges from 1 to %1$d. Higher values rotate with gentler shakes. In [%2$s], tap [Start] and shake as usual for %3$d s, and GOAT sets it so a slightly weaker shake will rotate the screen. If the screen rotates while you walk or toss in bed, lower the sensitivity.
When you lie on your side, Auto rotate turns the screen to landscape. With \'Shake to Rotate\' on, the current orientation stays until you shake the device.
Turning it off restores your previous Auto rotate setting.
Hold your phone upright and shake it to return to portrait. Just picking it up doesn\'t rotate the screen, so the orientation stays put even if you toss and turn in bed.

Screen rotation stays locked normally. Hold your device in the orientation you want and shake it, and the screen rotates that way, then locks again. Shake it while holding it upright to keep portrait. It vibrates to the rhythm of your shake when rotating.
Couldn\'t lock rotation. Check permission settings.
Shake your device to rotate the screen to its current orientation
The volume button direction isn\'t changed while you use a camera app, so you can still use the volume keys as a shutter.

Turn this on if the left button raises the volume when you rotate the device with the volume buttons on top. The default direction varies by device, like the Fold\'s main screen. When on, volume up and down are swapped in the opposite landscape orientation.

GOAT turns on an accessibility service with the system settings permission. This service only receives volume key presses and doesn\'t read screen content. Turning off the feature also disables it in the accessibility services list.

When you rotate the screen so the volume buttons are on top, the right button (relative to the screen) raises the volume and the left button lowers it. Even if you hold the device upside down, the top button raises the volume.
